label: header
text: THE CHINA MAIL.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hongkong Education.

label: text
text: (To the Editor of the China Mail).

label: text
text: Sir,—I have wondered, since local education has become a topic for discussion, how European ladies, diploma-ed or not, can ever hope to appreciate Chinese characteristics.

label: text
text: Now and then, I read of the number of qualified school-mistresses coming out to the Education Department. Some of the experts tell us that even an Oxford honours man has not got it in him to be able to adapt himself to understanding our traits and thereby making himself the most appropriate teacher. If so, how can the average diploma-ed schoolmistress do any better. Better it would be for all Hong Kong were to stick to the old system of a normal school for local Chinese youths and the University product but "and, this is a very great but, no difference in the status or salary of the two.

label: text
text:
WUN LUNG MINOR.
Hongkong, June 1.

label: paragraph_title
text: Plague of Bees.

label: paragraph_title
text: (To the Editor of the China Mail.)

label: text
text: Sir,—Through the courtesy of your columns I would like to ask whether the rearing of domestic bees comes under the Sanitary Department as an offensive trade or under the Police Department as a common nuisance? At any rate, this is the hiving season of bees and my house has been invaded by swarms of bees who are a great nuisance. Will those responsible take note that anybody keeping a domestic animal (in law, anything from a prehistoric monster to a mosquito) to the annoyance and/or danger of a neighbour is liable under an old Ordinance of the Colony?

label: text
text: Thanking you for the insertion of the above and enclosing my card,

label: text
text:
Yours, etc.,
CONDUIT ROAD.
Hongkong, June 2.

label: paragraph_title
text: FATAL LEAP.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUNDAY AFTERNOON'S TRAGEDY.

label: text
text: Pathetic circumstances attended the death of one of Messrs. A. S. Watson & Co.'s mineral water agents on Sunday afternoon when Mr. Mak Kip (35) of Macao jumped from a verandah and met his death. Mr. Mak, in addition to being agents for Messrs. Watson's, was employed by the Macao Electric Light Co. He had been ill for several months and had lately stayed with Mr. Peter Wong at No. 38a, Bonham Road, Breezy Point. On Sunday afternoon, while, it is believed; his mind was temporarily deranged, deceased either jumped or threw himself from the verandah.

label: text
text: Deceased was a very popular young man and leaves a wife and two children to mourn his loss. He had only been with Mr. and Mrs. Peter Wong for four days, for the benefit of his health, when the untimely event occurred to disturb the peace of mind of those who had his welfare at heart.

label: paragraph_title
text: FAREWELL

label: paragraph_title
text:
R. N. Y. POLICE MESS
CONCERT.

label: text
text: A very happy function took place at the R. N.Y. Police Mission Saturday night when a Dinner was given to a few of the Naval friends who are about to leave the Colony. Fitting toasts were given and responded to. Following the dinner a Smoking Concert was held under the Chairmanship of Mr. D. H. G. Smith. Petty Officer Probart proved an efficient entertainer in monologues and humorous songs. Ldg. Sea. Jack Mitchell upheld his reputation in some very catchy songs: Mr. T. Edwards contributed renderings of old time songs. Fresh talent was discovered in Sgt. Eddie McNay who, with his sweet mellow voice rendered "What God Made Mother For" but failed to respond to the call for an encore. Mr. J. Collins contributed to the programme and the chorus party in fine form. Mr. J. Callaghan assisted ably at the plano in accompanying many of the items.

label: paragraph_title
text: FALSE NAMES.

label: paragraph_title
text: SAILORS WHO CREATED TROUBLE.

label: paragraph_title
text: Tramcar Incidents.

label: text
text: Before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry, at the Central Magistracy this morning, three "American seamen were charged on two counts of evading payment of tramway fare and obstruction.

label: text
text:
There was some delay in the accused being brought into Court after they had been removed this morning from the custody of the Police by an escort from the U.S.S. Sacramento as it was found that they had given false names and stated that they belonged to the U.S.S. Pampanga. Their proper names were Jeff Cantrill, Harry A. Thorne and Irvine Coulter, all of the U.S.S. Helena.
A traffic officer of the Tramway Company giving evidence stated that he first saw the three accused in a car near the Ming Yuen gardens. They refused to pay the fare when called upon and gave him and the conductors considerable trouble, as well as causing inconvenience to the passengers by changing cars at Causeway Bay and again at Tin Lok Lane. Witness stated that at Bowrington bridge the third accused threatened to strike him. Witness and a Chinese constable kept up with the men after they had alighted near the bridge, and the latter went ahead later and laid information at No. 2 Police Station which resulted in the accused being taken into custody when they reached that point.

label: text
text:
The third accused denied that he threatened to assault witness. Asked by His Worship why they gave false names, all three said that they did it in order to hide their movements from the ship.
His Worship said that the evidence he had taken was sufficient to prove their guilt and fined each of the accused $10 and $25 on the two counts respectively.

label: paragraph_title
text: MOTOR TOUTS.

label: paragraph_title
text:
PRIVATE LICENCES
ABUSED.

label: text
text:
According to the "Wah Tsz Yat " Po," "tramp" motor-cars which now/ply for hire on the streets will soon be forbidden.
The vernacular paper explains that there are a number of motor-cars, each bought by a few adventurous spirits who run about town for hire by trips. These cars are registered under "private" licences and, as they have practically no overhead charges can operate at great profit.

label: text
text: REAPING A HARVEST.

label: text
text: Many a local resident has been accosted by youthful touts in the streets. Yesterday, a “China Mail” man who was given a “lift” in one such car, was told by the driver's assistant that they made over $25 a day and on Sunday night had to stop running because their petrol had given out. They had just bought a Dodge car for $2,550 and were confident of reaping a harvest. One advantage which the assistant pointed out was that they were no hours of restriction for cars with private licences and that the fees were much lower.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEW RENTS LAW.

label: text
text: The third reading of the Rents Amendment Bill which was the subject of yet further discussion at the last meeting of the Legislative Council is on the agenda of business for Thursday's meeting of the Legislative Council.

label: text
text: A resolution to be put to the Council is to the effect that the percentages on the valuation of tenements on the Kowloon Bay Reclamation, payable as rates, shall be 13 per cent on the following New Kowloon Inland Lot numbers: 132, 226, 227, 238, 239 and 251.

label: text
text: Jones was sent by his employer, a bookmaker, to collect a betting debt from Smith, who was notorious for his slackness in settling accounts. After listening to several excuses Jones remarked: "Well, at least let me know on what date I may expect payment." Smith replied: "Do you take me for a prophet?" "No," responded Jones. "Up to the present I have always regarded you as a loss!"

label: paragraph_title
text: SANDAKAN NOTES.

label: paragraph_title
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Sandakan has been gripped in a somewhat mild form of 'Flu' epidemic, for the last month or so. Padres, Teachers, and many Europeans as well as Native and Chinese including your correspondent were laid hors de combat for a number of days, but the sickness is gradually disappearing.

label: text
text: It is with regret I learn that on account of ill health His Excellence Major General Sir William Rycroft, K.C.B., K.C.M.G., had to tender his resignation as Governor of the State of British North Borneo. Sir William first arrived in this country to take up the appointment of Governor on November 21, 1922.

label: text
text: The following letter from His Excellency, Major General Sir William Rycroft, K.O.B., K.O.M.G., appears in the "Official Gazette" Extraordinary of May 13.

label: text
text:
After a little more than two and a half years in Borneo I am forced to relinquish my post under the highest medical orders.
It is with the greatest regret that I sever my connection with the State. On doing so I must tender my deepest thanks to the whole of the officials, European and Asiatic including Native Chiefs, who were responsible for having given me the happiest recollections of my period as Governor.

label: text
text: I am confident that there is a great future for the country, but patience is necessary.

label: text
text: I understand that Mr. A. G. Pearson, C.M.G., the former Governor, who is at present the Secretary, to the Chartered Company in London, will resume office as Governor temporarily. He is expected out towards the end of August; meantime the Honourable the Government Secretary Mr. F. W. Fraser, O.B.E., will act as Officer Administering the Govern

label: text
text: The Honourable the Resident of Sandakan Mr. H. N. L. Bumbury and Mrs. Bumbury left on the 21st by the s.s. Mau Sang via Hongkong on furlough for England and Mr. D. R. Maxwell will act as Acting President.

label: text
text: By the same boat Mr. Koh Peckpin, the Managing Partner of Chop Kim Eng Watt Bros.: the pioneer timber Merchant of Borneo, left to relieve his brother as Manager in the Hongkong branch of the same firm; he was accompanied by Mrs. Koh Peck-pin. Mr. S. A. Rahman, is temporarily in charge of Sandukan firm, until the arrival of Mr. Koh Peck-chick from Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Mr. J. George, Manager of Bakau Company and Mrs. George, left for the United Kingdom on

label: text
text: Mr. C. M. Stanhope returned from furlough and has taken over the Managership of the State Bank, Sandakan branch, from Mr. S. W. Matthews, who proceeded to England on leave.

label: text
text: The many friends of Rev. T. C. Alexander will be pleased to learn of his excellent recovery from a bad stroke of Flu. He has now been discharged from the Hospital.

label: text
text: Capt. Pearson, Superintendent of Sandakan Police, Mr. S. W. Matthews of the State Bank and Capt. Campbell of the U.S. Kinabalu have all been in the Hospital recently, but I am pleased to learn they are all out again.

label: text
text: Another old Borneo landmark Mr. Chan, late, on the China of Sandakan has crossed the world of mist, he died in his native home in Swatow. Mr. Chan, to-pin, was one of the pioneer settlers in Borneo. At one time and before coming South to make his fortune, he was an Assistant in the late Indian firm of Messrs. Taria-Topan, Opium and yarn merchants in Hongkong, whose Manager was the late Md. Khetsey. As Capitan China and a Chinese gentleman, he was well liked and respected by Government Officials, European Merchants as well as Chinese and Native. He was kind to all, of a quiet and unassuming disposition and his word as a Chinese merchant was as good as his bond. He passed away in his native home in Swatow at a ripe old age, an octogenarian, in the presence of his wife, sons and grand-sons, who left Sandakan and reached home in time to be present at his death-bed.

text: HEAD CUT OFF

label: paragraph_title
text: GRUESOME WONG NEI CHUNG DISCOVERY.

label: text
text: A gruesome discovery was made at a garden in Wong Nel Chung village, near the new filter beds, when the Police removed to the mortuary yesterday the body of an unknown Chinese about 24 years old. The head was completely severed from the trunk, and the circumstances point to murder.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE NEW KISMET.

label: paragraph_title
text:
BEAUTIFUL SCENIC
EFFECTS.

label: text
text: 一

label: text
text: It was as a spectacle that "Kismet" made its appeal when it was produced at the Garrick Theatre in 1911. It is as a spectacle that it must succeed or fail, as it was revived at the New Oxford Theatre.

label: text
text: But the manner of the revival is entirely different from the manner of the original production. Instead of the old, flamboyant mounting is seen something subtle in lighting effects, something that bears close relationship with that which is connected with the arts of the Cubists and the Futurists.

label: text
text: The story itself is nothing more nor less than a prop for a series of stage pictures.

label: text
text: Yet, after all, Edward Kno-block has a good tale to tell, and it seemed to be followed with in-terest. The scene is laid in the Baghdad of “The Arabian Nights,” and many strange things happen in a very brief period. How Haji, the beggar, is made a prince and sinks again to the depths is told in lines which are at odd moments apparently intended to be pactical, but which do not lift the play above its spectacular appeal.

label: text
text: Mr. Sam Livesay is the new Haji—a part originally played by Mr. Oscar Asche. Mr. Livesay acts with a certain power, but it appears obvious that once upon a time he saw Oscar Asche in the part. All round, the acting is more than adequate—but the scenic effects matter more than the cast.

label: paragraph_title
text: MYSTIFIED SCIENTISTS.

label: paragraph_title
text: A MAN WITH SIX SENSES.

label: text
text: 一

label: text
text: What is the strange occult power possessed by Louis Kahn, the "Man with the Sixth Sense"?

label: text
text: His case is inexplicable to the foremost French scientists, and a former French Premier. Academicians, High Court judges, and detectives have been mystified by a display of his uncanny power. He is able to read a letter written by another person without seeing or touching it.

label: text
text: Kahn, who is 53 and a German who disarows German nationality, has just demonstrated his powers before an audience including M. Louis Barthou, a French ex-Premier; M. Loucheur, a former Cabinet Minister; and M. Morain, the Prefect of Police.

label: text
text: There were twelve persons in all present and each wrote in an adjoining room a phrase on a slip of paper which was folded eight times and kept in the closed hand.

label: text
text: He left the room while the ships were exchanged, and on returning said: "Though you have been exchanging your slips each one finally came back to its author." This was correct.

label: text
text: Then he told those present what they had written.

label: text
text: With the exception of an error in one word, which did not alter the sense of the phrase, Kahn faithfully rendered the contents of the twelve slips.

label: text
text: Striking proof of his telepathic powers was shown when, at M. Barthou's suggestion, a woman in the company wrote on her slip of paper a declaration of affection for a well known politician.

label: text
text: Madame, please burn your slip, far away from me so that I cannot possibly see it," said Kahn, and when the woman had done so, he pointed to M. Barthou, remarking: "The gentleman there dictated the phrase to you, so he will be able to certify if I renter it correctly." And, amid laughter, he read word for word what the woman had written.

label: paragraph_title
text: SHANGHAI RIOTING.

label: text
text: The students here held a meeting yesterday afternoon in the Central Park to discuss the Shanghai affair.

label: text
text: The speakers declared that the affair was a national one affecting the whole of the Chinese people.

label: text
text: Further meetings were arranged for to-day at which it is expected resolutions will be passed demanding the restoration of the foreign concessions, the abolition of extra-territoriality and the Mixed Court in Shanghai, also of the foreign police stations in Shanghai, and the punishment of the police who shot the students.

label: paragraph_title
text: Chinese Demands.

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, June 2.

label: text
text: The Chinese Foreign Commissioner presented the following demands to the Consular Body in Shanghai:—

label: text
text: Release of the arrested rioters, compensation for deaths, and punishment of those responsible therefor.

label: text
text: A meeting of consuls to consider the above has been called for June 6.

label: text
text: The Peking Government is not officially connected with the demands.

label: paragraph_title
text: Strike Begins.

label: text
text: Prisoners were taken to the Mixed Court this morning heavily escorted. The route was guarded by Volunteers and police. There were no disturbances.

label: text
text: It was a subdued looking group of 45 rioters who appeared before the Chinese magistrate and American assessor.

label: text
text: Evidence of arrest was given and the case remanded. Light bail was accepted.

label: text
text: There were a few unimportant isturbances in the outlying districts this morning, including the mobbing of a Japanese constable whom the rioters threw into a creek before assistance arrived.

label: text
text: The strike is taking denite form insomuch as the fresh food markets did not open to-day.

label: paragraph_title
text: THEATRE.

label: paragraph_title
text: LILLIAN GISH IN "THE WHITE SISTER."

label: text
text: Miss Gish is magnificent! No actress of this generation on stage or screen has carried the flame of sheer genius into her acting as does the frail little star of "The White Sister" now showing at the Queen's Theatre.

label: text
text: In filming F. Marion Crawford's story, the Director took a company to Italy. Studios and laboratories were established, and then began the making of what should prove one of truly great productions in cinema history.

label: text
text: Most persons are familiar with the story and many have undoubtedly longed for its presentation on the screen. The story, offering many thrills in the way of the actual eruption of Vesuvius, and a flood that sweeps away an Italian town has been closely followed. The settings are exquisite, the photography of the highest quality and Miss Gisk's supporting cast shows it was chosen with care, for the members all contribute to the general effectiveness of the film.
